about: slapstic page 2 $85EC-$89FF: the wave 1 probots - set-up of the five records at ALIEN for the wave and for the training manual, spawning, the per-frame move loop, the head, spin and bob animation, the behaviour state table and the code that picks a new behaviour

P2:85EC.name: probot_setup
P2:85EC.desc: wave 1 set-up of the probots, called once from wave1_setup (phase $45) through maze entry MZ_859E. loads the points of objects 4-7 and 9-$10 into math RAM through the cross-bank JADOBJ entry L60A8 (B = object number), keeping the math RAM address before and after objects 9-$10 in w1_anim_pts and w1_anim_end for the point animation at P2_8E86, then frees all five $1A-byte records at ALIEN and presets each one's height ($0200), spin angle and rate and part mask from the table at P2_866C, state 4 and both timers 8. ends with w1_spawn = 5 so that probots_move fills the records one per frame

P2:8684.name: probot_spawn
P2:8684.desc: brings the free record at U to life: type 7, flags 0, and a place on the far edge of the square round the player - by the sign of a random byte either x or y gets $8000 added and the other axis gets a random value in -$4000..$3FFF - then state 2 (close in on the player). called by probots_move, which clears x and y first

P2:86C7.name: man_probot_setup
P2:86C7.desc: training manual set-up of the demo probot, called from man_init_probot through maze entry MZ_825C with B = manual page 0-2 (anything higher is taken as 0). fills the first record at ALIEN from the 10-byte row of the table at P2_875E for that page (x, y, height, spin angle and rate, part mask, type), state 0 so that it holds still, frees the other four records, loads objects 4-7 and 9-$10 into math RAM as probot_setup does, and sets w1_spawn to 0 so that nothing is spawned

P2:877C.name: probots_move
P2:877C.desc: per-frame move of the wave 1 probots, called through maze entry MZ_837F from wave1_exec (phase $1A), wave1_end_exec (phase $1C) and the manual's man_move_probot. with w1_spawn above 0 it spawns one probot in the first free record among the first w1_spawn records, with w1_spawn minus it frees every record that is not in view (flag $10 of byte 1 clear). then it counts the live records into w1_active and for each one runs the head, spin and bob animation, the behaviour, the point animation (P2_8E86) and the two timers (P2_8F9A)

P2:87E2.name: probot_turn_bob
P2:87E2.desc: animation of the probot record at U. the head angle (byte $10) moves by a quarter of its rate (byte $11) each frame: while the angle is more than $20 from the target (byte $12) the rate grows away from zero, up to $11 or down to $F3, and within $20 of the target a rate of exactly +1 or -1 takes a new random target and reverses (probot_head_back, probot_head_fwd), any other rate is left as it is. the body spin angle (byte 11) advances by its rate (byte 12), and the bob offset (word at 13) counts up and down between 0 and $2F, reversing its direction byte (15) at either end

P2:884F.name: probot_head_fwd
P2:884F.desc: gives the probot at U a new random head target angle (byte $12 from RND_S1), reverses its bob direction (byte 15) and sets the head rate to +1

P2:8861.name: probot_head_back
P2:8861.desc: as probot_head_fwd with the head rate set to -1

P2:88A7.name: probot_pick_state
P2:88A7.desc: picks a new behaviour for the probot at U by calling one state start routine, which stores the state number in byte 4 and may set a goal or speed. state 0 (the manual's demo probot) is left alone. with w1_spawn minus (end of the wave) it is P2_8A9D, state 11, fly off and free the record. a probot that is out of view and not already in state 9 gets P2_8C14, state 9, a goal in front of the player. otherwise during the first 150 frames of the phase (PH_TIM below $96) the entry of the 4-word table at P2_889F for w1_level and 3 is used, and after that a random one of the ten entries of the table at P2_888B

P2:88F0.name: probot_behave
P2:88F0.desc: per-frame behaviour of the probot at U. on every fourth frame with one chance in eight it picks a new behaviour (probot_pick_state), then it calls the handler of the current state: byte 4 of the record indexes the table of twelve routine addresses at P2_8873, a state above 11 is run as state 2. unless the state is 0 it then eases the height (probot_height) and, when the position is held relative to the player and is within $0200 of him on both axes, starts state 3 (P2_8A3E, back away). X is preserved

P2:8942.name: probot_height
P2:8942.desc: eases the height of the probot at U (word at 9) a quarter of the way to $0200 plus eight times its bob offset (word at 13)

P2:8954.name: probot_drift
P2:8954.desc: moves the player-relative position of the probot at U (words at 5 and 7) against the player's motion: the matrix processor's perspective multiply (MS_PERS) scales the player's speeds s1_vx and s1_vy by a quarter of the sum of the sizes of the probot's x and y, and the products are subtracted from x and y. used by the state handlers that keep the position relative to the player

P2:898D.name: probot_goal_drift
P2:898D.desc: as probot_drift, but the scaled player speeds are subtracted from the probot's goal position (words at $15 and $17) and not from its own position. used by the go-to-goal states 6, 7 and 9

P2:89CA.name: probot_set_hold
P2:89CA.desc: makes the position of the probot at U relative to the player (P2_8E54) and stores state 0, hold still. nothing calls or points to it: dead code. the manual set-up stores state 0 itself

P2:89D2.name: probot_st_hold
P2:89D2.desc: state 0 handler: only makes the position relative to the player (P2_8E54), so the probot stays where it is in front of him. the state of the training manual's demo probot, which probot_pick_state never changes

P2:89D6.name: probot_set_drift
P2:89D6.desc: state start routine, entry 0 of the table at P2_888B: stores state 1 (drift) in byte 4 of the record at U

P2:89DB.name: probot_st_drift
P2:89DB.desc: state 1 handler: makes the position relative to the player and drifts it against the player's motion (probot_drift). when the probot is out of view it picks a new behaviour

P2:89EB.name: probot_set_fixed
P2:89EB.desc: state start routine, entry 3 of the table at P2_888B and entry 0 of the table at P2_889F, also called by probot_setup for every record: stores state 4 (stay at a fixed place) in byte 4 of the record at U

P2:89F0.name: probot_st_fixed
P2:89F0.desc: state 4 handler: makes the position absolute (P2_8E6D adds the player's position once and sets bit $08 of the type byte), so the probot stays at one place on the ground while the player moves. when it is out of view it picks a new behaviour

P2:89FD.name: probot_set_close
P2:89FD.desc: state start routine, entry 1 of the table at P2_888B, also called by probot_spawn: stores state 2 (close in on the player) in byte 4 of the record at U

4855.name: rnd_s4
4855.desc: fourth saved random byte: rnd_set moves the previous RND_S2 here when it stores the old RND_S1 and RND_S2 as a word at RND_S3. page 2 uses it as one more random byte, in probot_pick_state to pick one of the ten state start routines

4CAF.name: w1_anim_pts
4CAF.desc: word: math RAM address (BJ_RAM) taken by the probot set-up after objects 4-7 are loaded, so the first of the 8-byte point records of objects 9-$10. P2_8E86 starts its per-frame point animation here

4CB1.name: w1_anim_end
4CB1.desc: word: math RAM address (BJ_RAM) taken by the probot set-up after object $10 is loaded, the end of the point records that P2_8E86 animates

questions: P2:89CA - nothing calls or points to this routine (store state 0 after making the position relative): taken as dead code

P2:866C - the table holds six 4-byte rows ($866C-$8683) but probot_setup reads only five, one per record, and uses only the first three bytes of a row. the sixth row looks like a leftover of a six-record version

P2:875E - the type byte of the manual rows is $01, $01 and $11. bits $02 (may shoot) and $04 (may transmit) are tested by the view code at P2_915F and P2_9175, bit $08 means absolute position. what bits $01 and $10 of the type byte mean was not found in this stretch

P2:87F9 - near the head's target angle the DECB / INCB result is never stored back to byte $11, so only a rate of exactly +1 or -1 picks a new target, and a rate of 0 with the angle within $20 of the target never changes. it looks like a slip in the original code. described as the code runs

49D2 - the probot record at ALIEN ($1A bytes, five records $49D2-$4A53) as read from this stretch and its callees: 0 type and flag bits (0 = free), 1 per-frame flags ($10 in view, $80 lined up), 3 timer, 4 behaviour state, 5 x, 7 y, 9 height (words), 11 spin angle, 12 spin rate, 13 bob offset (word), 15 bob direction, $10 head angle, $11 head rate, $12 head target, $13 part mask, $14 timer, $15 and $17 goal position or speed (words). the offsets have no names in the defines
5098 - used as the player's x position next to s1_ty by the routines this stretch calls (P2_8E54, P2_8E6D), it has no name in the defines. it is outside this range, so not named here
